headline: Artificial intelligence crossed a line as the JadePuffer agent ran an entire ransomware attack on its own, while North Korea flooded open-source registries with 108 malicious packages.

emerging_trends.text: Large language models now run intrusions on their own, and the JadePuffer operation drove a full ransomware attack from initial breach to database wipe with no human at the keyboard.
emerging_trends.topic_title: JadePuffer AI Agent Runs Full Ransomware Attack

emerging_trends.text: North Korea's Contagious Interview crews are industrializing open-source poisoning, flooding npm, Packagist, Go, and Chrome with 108 malicious packages under the PolinRider banner.
Vendors racing to bolt AI features onto shipping products keep generating vulnerabilities that rank high-risk more often and linger unpatched longer than anything else.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Features Pile Up Security Debt

topics.title: AI Features Pile Up Security Debt
topics.latest_developments: Help Net Security's July 5 week-in-review flagged a hardening pattern: the vulnerabilities that AI and LLM features introduce rank high-risk far more often than other flaws and take longer to fix.
topics.summary: As vendors bolt AI capabilities onto existing products, the resulting flaws skew severe and linger; security teams should fold AI features into the same threat models and patch cadence as core code.

sources.title: Week in review: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited, Oracle EBS Payments flaw under attack

topics.title: PolinRider Floods Open-Source Registries
topics.latest_developments: North Korea's Contagious Interview actors published 108 malicious packages and browser extensions across npm, Packagist, Go, and Chrome under the PolinRider label on July 4, and JFrog flagged two of them, rollup-packages-polyfill-core and rollup-runtime-polyfill-core, that impersonate the legitimate rollup-plugin-polyfill-node to plant remote access and steal developer secrets.
topics.summary: The Contagious Interview operation, tied to North Korea, poisons software supply chains by publishing counterfeit developer packages that mimic real tooling down to their metadata; developers should verify provenance and lock dependencies. The campaign stays active as attackers keep compromising maintainer accounts.

sources.title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign
North Korea-Linked npm Packages Mimic Rollup Polyfills to Steal Developer Secrets

topics.title: JadePuffer AI Agent Runs Full Ransomware Attack
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek this week detailed how the JadePuffer agent chained a Langflow remote-code-execution exploit with real-time reasoning to steal credentials, move laterally, and encrypt and wipe a production database, the first ransomware intrusion a large language model ran start to finish.
topics.summary: JadePuffer shows an AI agent can plan and carry out a multistage ransomware attack on its own; organizations running Langflow should patch the remote-code-execution flaw and restrict what network reach they grant AI tools.

sources.title: JadePuffer ransomware used AI agent to automate entire attack
Agentic AI Used to Conduct Ransomware Attack via Langflow

topics.title: Apple Hide My Email Leaks Real Addresses
topics.latest_developments: Wired's July 4 security roundup reported that Apple's Hide My Email, the iCloud+ feature that hands users disposable relay addresses, fails to conceal their real address in some cases.
topics.summary: Hide My Email sells as an iCloud+ privacy tool that masks a subscriber's true address behind random relays; the reported failure means users should stop treating the relay as guaranteed anonymity.

sources.title: Security Roundup: Apple's Hide My Email Service Fails to Hide Your Email

business_politics.title: Ukraine Drone Strikes Ignite Russian Fuel Crisis
business_politics.latest_developments: Kyiv has intensified its drone campaign against Russian refineries and pipelines to an unprecedented rate, driving what the Financial Times calls Russia's worst fuel crisis in decades.
business_politics.summary: Ukraine's escalating strikes on Russian energy infrastructure have choked domestic fuel supplies across Russia, a deepening shortage that feeds into global crude markets already jittery after the Iran war.

business.title: Sojourner House Wins $150K Grant
business.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh nonprofit Sojourner House landed a $150,000 grant to keep supporting mothers through substance-use treatment.
business.summary: Sojourner House, a Pittsburgh nonprofit that lets mothers stay with their children during recovery, will use the $150,000 grant to sustain its substance-use treatment programs.

around_town.title: Parkway East Closure Begins This Week
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT's 25-day full closure of the Parkway East begins this week, on July 10, to replace the Commercial Street Bridge.
around_town.summary: PennDOT will shut the Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit for 25 days to replace the aging Commercial Street Bridge near Frick Park, forcing detours on thousands of daily commuters.

sources.title: Ready or not, Pittsburgh, the 25-day Parkway East closure begins this week

around_town.title: Heat Wave Breaks, Storms Linger
around_town.latest_developments: The heat wave ended over the weekend, but Sunday, July 5, brings more rain and storms after Saturday's severe weather knocked out power to thousands across the region.
around_town.summary: Saturday's storms downed trees and wires and cut power to thousands of customers around Pittsburgh, and forecasters flagged Sunday, July 5, as another impact day with heavy downpours and gusty winds even as temperatures and humidity eased.

team_usa.title: US Teen Tate Taylor Wins Prefontaine 200
team_usa.latest_developments: American teenager Tate Taylor upset a field that included Olympic 200-meter champion Letsile Tebogo to win the 200 at the Prefontaine Classic.
team_usa.summary: At the Prefontaine Classic, U.S. teenager Tate Taylor stunned a loaded 200-meter field, beating Botswana's Olympic gold medalist Letsile Tebogo in a signal performance for a rising American sprinter.

reading.title: The AI Industry Is Losing
reading.summary: Zitron argues the AI industry is losing, contending the economics of the build-out do not add up and the sector's promoters are running short of ways to disguise it.
